source.title: Sparse Autoencoder Insights on Voice Embeddings
source.authors: Dan Pluth; Yu Zhou; V. Gurbani

record.tranche_reason: The study tests sparse-autoencoder latent features in Titanet speaker embeddings, not neuron poles or any of the claim versions. Its results are relevant to the broader idea of interpretable features, but the measured units are SAE latents rather than the model's own neurons.
record.gate_note: The reported classification and steering results concern SAE latent features in audio speaker embeddings, not neuron poles. They are recorded with versions ["none"] as related findings; they do not test any listed version. The paper discusses prior SAE work on language models, but cited results from those works are not included.
record.test_reason: The study trains TopK sparse autoencoders on 192-d Titanet speaker embeddings and evaluates SAE latents, not the model's own neurons or neuron explanations. It asserts the raw embeddings are 'dense and not clearly interpretable' and that the features are 'not evident in the original embedding'. It never measures per-dimension or per-neuron interpretability, so the premise is assumed rather than tested. No version (neuron-pole shares, scale, InceptionV1, architecture or tools, neuron circuits, explanation scoring) is addressed. 'assumes' fits better than 'discusses' because the paper never discusses the neuron-cleanliness claim itself.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude SAEs extract mono-semantic, steerable features (language, music) from Titanet speaker embeddings. They say these features show LLM-like properties: identification, splitting and steering (Anthropic points 1–4). Universality is left for future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains TopK sparse autoencoders on 192-element Titanet speaker embeddings, identifies features using logistic-regression probes, and tests steering of reconstructed embeddings. It does not audit neuron poles or test explanations of neuron activations.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature-identification performance varies with SAE latent dimension and TopK. The authors report language-feature splitting as latent dimensionality grows; the point where it occurs varies with K. Music classification performance drops for models with low K.

fits_no_version.finding: Logistic-regression-selected SAE latents in Titanet speaker embeddings discriminate Spanish vs English and music vs voice on held-out data, and toggling them shifts reconstructed embeddings toward the other class.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents on non-transformer audio embeddings can isolate and steer binary attributes such as language and hold music.

fits_no_version.finding: The single Spanish latent splits into Spanish-male and Spanish-female latents as SAE latent dimension grows (around 300), regardless of K.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature splitting occurs in audio speaker-embedding SAEs as dictionary size grows.

record.peer_reviewed: 2025 Conference on Artificial Intelligence x Multimedia (AIxMM)
record.problems: The study does not directly test neuron interpretability. The authors report that direct listening-based feature identification was difficult and instead use labeled language and music datasets with logistic-regression probes. The SAE latent space examined is at most approximately 3x the input dimension, which the authors contrast with much larger latent spaces in LLM studies. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the listed results.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results omitted. Figure-based grid-search curves are not separately rowed because the text gives only qualitative summaries for those sweeps.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B or any LLM neuron poles; no one-job, two-job or unexplained shares.
No neuron-share comparison across language models, MoE architectures or scale.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron reanalysis.
No interpretable-neuron shares across architectures, regularization or tools.
No attribution graphs built from neurons.
No test of activating-example explanations against firing prediction.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: Rows correctly carry versions ['none']. R1 and R2 report the performance of a latent chosen on the training split and evaluated on a separate test split. The grid-search figures (recall near 70% for most models) show these values are favourable picks of one SAE configuration. Direct listening-based identification of latents largely failed, but that concerns SAE latents, not neurons. No baselines on raw embedding dimensions were run, so the paper gives no evidence on neuron or dimension interpretability.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or estimates of one-job, two-job, or not-understood shares.
No comparison of neuron interpretability shares across language models, dense and mixture-of-experts architectures, or model scales.
No analysis of InceptionV1 neurons, cat-and-car examples, pose, or recursive generalization.
No estimate of interpretable neuron shares across architectures, regularization methods, tools, or vision-model scales.
No attribution graphs or test of whether a model's own neurons suffice as circuit units.
No test of whether explanations fit activating examples but fail to predict other activations.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.
